title: Simulation of a mapped computation
statement: Let $M$ be a finite Turing machine over the Boolean alphabet, let $x$ and $y$ be Boolean words, and let $c$ be a configuration of $M$ on input $y$. Suppose a Boolean tag correctly marks the boundary of the input-head position of $c$. For any input-head position $p$ on $x$, Boolean word $a$, output prefix $pre$, and time $t\in\mathbb{N}$, there is a tag for the input-head position of the configuration reached by running $M$ from $c$ for $t$ steps, correctly marking its boundary, such that the run for $t$ steps of the constructed machine on the corresponding virtual configuration equals the virtual configuration associated with that reached configuration, with $p$, $a$, and $pre$ unchanged.
hypotheses_covered: $M$ is a finite Turing machine over Booleans
$c$ is a configuration of $M$ on input $y$
the given tag correctly marks the boundary of $c$'s input-head position
$p$ is a valid input-head position on $x$
